meta.title: AI i18n: a multilingual Astro template
meta.description: An Astro template where English is the source, the other languages are generated by AI Glot, and a lock file tells you which translations have gone out of date.

hero.title: Write one language. Publish four.
hero.body: This site is the demo and the documentation at once. It is published in English, French, German and Spanish, and every word you read outside the English version was produced by a single command and reviewed in a diff.

features.title: What the template actually solves
features.body: Translating a site once is easy. These are the three problems that show up afterwards.

items.title: Out of date is a fact, not a feeling
items.body: A lock file stores the hash of the English text each translation was made from, so the tooling can tell never translated from translated, then the English moved. Change one sentence and it reports exactly what is now behind, in every language.

items.title: Every language answers for every page
items.body: A page nobody has translated yet still exists in that language. It serves the English text with a notice and a canonical pointing home, or it redirects, and switching between the two is one word in a config file.

items.title: One batch, not one per language
items.body: Everything behind travels in a single AI Glot batch: one analysis, one plan, one approval. The translator sees the whole site at once, which is what keeps a term consistent between a menu label and the page it opens.

items.label: ways to treat an untranslated page

cta.title: Take it and change the copy
cta.body: Replace the English, set your languages in one config file, run one command. Nothing under src/ or scripts/ needs editing to change language, copy or behaviour.

meta.title: About this project
meta.description: What this Astro template ships, the one decision it is built around, and what it does not pretend to do.

about.title: About this project
about.lead: astro-ai-i18n is an open-source Astro template for sites that publish in several languages. English is authored by hand; French, German and Spanish are generated through the AI Glot CLI, written back as ordinary files, and reviewed like any other change.

sections.title: The one decision
sections.body: English is the source and nobody edits a generated file. The way to change the French is to change the English and run the translation again. A hand fix to a generated file is lost on the next run, silently, which is why the rule is absolute rather than a preference.

sections.title: Where the review happens
sections.body: Machine translation is acceptable here because a person reads the diff before it ships. That is the whole safety mechanism, and it is why the workflow writes plain files into the repository instead of calling an API at build time.

sections.title: What it does not do
sections.body: It does not detect the visitor's language or redirect them, it does not localize URLs, and it does not promise the translations are perfect. It makes the gap between languages visible and cheap to close, which is the part that usually rots.

items.title: The status command
items.body: One command reports what is missing, what went out of date and what it would cost in credits, before anything is sent.

items.title: The translation command
items.body: Sends exactly what is behind, in one batch for every language, then writes the results back into the files and updates the lock.

items.title: The fallback machinery
items.body: Untranslated pages serve English with a notice, or redirect. Either way they canonicalise to the English URL and are never advertised as that language.

items.title: The agent manual
items.body: An AGENTS.md that walks an assistant through installing AI Glot, choosing between the CLI and the REST API, and the mistakes this shape of site tends to make.
